overview.eyebrow: For councils, tourist offices and local businesses
overview.title: Your region’s places and events on one map — no app.
overview.lead: Visitors open it on their phone, filter, and go. You share one link.
overview.introP1: HelloLocal is a browser-based local tourism map. It brings a region’s sights, services, hospitality, special places and events onto one screen. No app to install, no account to browse, no hopping between websites.
overview.introP2: A region is more than its famous landmarks. Family cellars, craft workshops, tucked-away restaurants and local producers deserve a shared, easy-to-share presence. Place owners write their own pages; the council or tourist office passes everything on with a single link.
overview.differenceKicker: Why it is not just another map
overview.differenceTitle: Not the world atlas — your neighbourhood
overview.differenceLead: Google Maps lists everything. HelloLocal puts what visitors actually look for in your area into their hands: local places, fresh events, written by the people who run them — on one link you can share.
overview.seoTitle: HelloLocal | Interactive tourism map for municipalities
overview.seoDescription: Interactive tourism map for councils, tourist offices and local businesses. Sights, events, multiple languages — in the browser, no app required.
overview.keywords: interactive tourism map, digital tourism map, destination map, local events map, tourist office software, municipal tourism, DMO platform, multilingual tourism map, regional tourism map, local business listing, HelloLocal
overview.shotCaption: Szeged on the map: places, filters and upcoming events on one screen.
overview.statsApp: guests open it in the browser
overview.featuresTitle: What guests can use right away
overview.featuresLead: Opening hours, what’s on today — and the place that isn’t on the main square. One map, in the guest’s language.

hidden.title: What only locals used to know
hidden.text: Courtyards, workshops, market stalls, cellars — one turn off the high street. They go on the map so guests can find them, instead of vanishing in a world atlas.

traffic.title: One link for official and tourism channels
traffic.text: Website, newsletter, QR code, poster. A coherent presence from a modest budget — without building an ad machine.

region.title: Country → region → town → place
region.text: Several settlements can share one system, each with its own audience. Smaller towns do not have to build a full tourism site alone.

overview.storiesLead: Guests explore. Businesses look after their own pages. Councils and tourist offices present the whole offer with a single link.
overview.closingTitle: Show your region on one map.
overview.closingText: Open the live example and picture your own places on those pins: the workshop, the cellar, the service, or the whole area.
overview.closingImageAlt: A hiker with a yellow backpack on a mountain trail

collect.title: People who were missing go on the map
collect.text: Workshop, shop, cellar, service — with their own page, photos and opening hours. A presence guests are happy to forward.

publish.title: Events stay up to date
publish.text: What’s on this weekend stays in front. What’s finished drops off on its own — no manual tidy-up.

share.title: One link for the guest
share.text: Optionally on your own domain (for example helloetyek.hu), in their language. They open it on the phone, filter, and go — no new app.

app.q: Does a guest have to download an app?
app.a: No. The map and events open in the browser — on phone and desktop. Sign-in is only needed if they want to leave a rating.

languages.q: Is there a separate page for every language?
languages.a: Yes: Hungarian, English and German. Content is looked after per language — not one-click machine translation. Search finds each version on its own address.

editors.a: Whoever runs the place: the maker, the service, or staff at the council or tourist office. Everyone looks after their own part. An AI helper can draft copy if you get stuck — and we never sell visitors’ personal data.

towns.q: Can several settlements share one system?
towns.a: Yes. One region can bring several towns together. Each keeps its own map and programme; the guest stays where they arrived.

maps.a: Google Maps shows the world. HelloLocal shows your region: local places with their own introductions, fresh events, optional own domain — and one link you can put in tourism materials. Not an advertising marketplace, and you don’t push a new app onto guests.

places.title: Workshops show up too
places.text: With opening hours and their own page — easy to forward. Lesser-known spots are visible, not only the main square.

events.title: The weekend programme stays in front
events.text: What’s finished comes off. What’s on now is what guests see first — including a spontaneous weekend.

map.title: A map you can leave from
map.text: They see what’s open, what’s good in the rain, what’s on today. Works on the phone — no registration to browse.

languages.title: Guests read in their own language
languages.text: Content is written for the guest’s language, on the address they search. Same map — three languages.

sites.title: Several towns, separate programmes
sites.text: One region can cover more than one place. Each map and programme stays distinct — guests don’t slip into the next town by accident.

editors.title: Whoever runs the place writes it
editors.text: The maker, the service or the town team looks after their own copy. AI can help draft it, and they see traffic — guests see what’s true right now.

maker.title: The workshop gets its own page
maker.text: Ceramics, textiles, jam, honey. Photos, opening hours — and a page guests can send on to friends.
maker.alt: Handmade ceramic bowls on a workshop table

service.title: Your name comes first
service.text: Hairdresser, tailor, bike shop, massage. Guests look at the area — and find your name and address, not a distant generic list.
service.alt: A small bicycle workshop with tools and a wheel on the bench

quiet.title: One corner further in
quiet.text: Courtyard, workshop, market stall — off the main street. Places only locals knew go on the map too.
quiet.alt: An open courtyard gate on a quiet side street

town.title: The one who can bring them together
town.text: You gather local businesses and pass them to the visitor on a single link — in the guest’s language, ready for campaigns and the website.
town.alt: A live map of local places and events
